pr_body:
Fix #74802

### Issue fixed

Commenting a folded function didn't comment the content of the function if at last line of the selection.

![bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3649998/226114298-04a1684e-0559-42c3-87ca-959a290a6dc6.gif)

### Fix proposal

If last commented line  via CTRL+K is a folded, also comment inner folded content.

![comment_folded_function](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3649998/226114350-0168d19f-3b25-4cb1-84b9-09864bcc2e2f.gif)

Note : If selection was not ending on a folded line but contains a folded part, comment inside was correctly commented.
pr_comments:
> This breaks when using multi carets as it no longer keeps track of the last changed line. So if there are 2 carets on the same line, no comment will be toggled.

Oh sorry. I had misunderstood the purpose of the last_line variable. It should be better now.

![multicarret](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3649998/227733274-a9f43b85-c048-493a-b30d-3876fa65f07d.gif)

issue_context.title: Commenting collapsed function not working properly
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 stable

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

If select and comment collapsed function, only the first line will be commented.

![comments bug](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5310985/224521105-1f98d79b-28b7-4d79-9b4f-eb189e4603da.gif)


### Steps to reproduce

Collapse function.
Select line with mouse,
Press Ctrl + K
Expand collapsed function

You will see that all lines are not commented.

### Minimal reproduction project

```
func dummy() -> void:
	print (1)
	print (2)
	print (3)
```

review_comments: `last_line = to` above, does it need to be set after this instead?

I don't think so.

In the loop, ``last_line`` need to be the set at the real caret line to prevent issue when pair number of carets are on the same line and would lead to comment and then uncomment the same part of code (and so no visible action will occur because the second [or any other pair number] caret will undo what the first [or unpair number] would have done.
